summary:
Public Law 118-232 has the single operative purpose of removing the federal statutory restriction on amendment or modification of the Constitution of American Samoa. It accomplishes that purpose solely by repeal: section 1 repeals section 12 of Public Law 98-213, codified at 48 U.S.C. § 1662a.

The repealed provision was the codified congressional restriction governing amendments or modifications to the Constitution of American Samoa. By repealing 48 U.S.C. § 1662a, the Act eliminates that statutory requirement and restores the framework referenced in the Act’s title: administration of federal territorial law in American Samoa as delegated to the President and, under Executive Order 10264 of June 29, 1951, to the Secretary of the Interior, under which the Constitution of American Samoa was approved and may be amended without further congressional action, subject to Congress’s authority under the Territorial Clause, U.S. Const. art. IV, § 3, cl. 2.

The Act contains no new affirmative approval of any specific constitutional amendment, no substitute amendment procedure, no delegation of additional authority, and no conforming amendments to other provisions of title 48 or any other statute. It imposes no conditions precedent, deadlines, reporting requirements, or implementing regulations. It contains no authorization of appropriations and makes no appropriation. It includes no sunset provision or special effective-date clause; accordingly, the repeal takes effect upon enactment, January 4, 2025.
